raw_case_text:
A 66-year-old man with stage IIIIC lung squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) (cT4N3M0) presented with cough and chest pain for four months ( Figure 1 ). He had a history of smoking for more than 40 years (40 cigarettes a day, quit > 3 months). His body weight was 71 kg, with no significant change from the previous weight. No sensitive gene mutations were detected and the percentage of tumor cells with membranous PD-L1 staining (tumor proportion score) was 30%. Four cycles of tislelizumab plus nab-paclitaxel and carboplatin chemotherapy were performed. The fourth cycle of treatment were synchronized with thoracic radiotherapy (TRT) (60 Gy/30 fractions), the mean lung dose (MLD) was 8.07 Gy, 22.5% of the lung received 20 Gy (V20), and 36% of the lung received 5 Gy (V5), which ended in Jan 2022 ( Figure 2C ). The patient's symptoms of cough and chest pain improved.
After 20 weeks of the initial tislelizumab administration (20 days after radiotherapy ended), dyspnea and cough developed. The patient presented to our hospital, the laboratory tests including hemogram and inflammatory markers were normal except for the white blood cell of 14.79x109/L. Computerized tomography (CT) of the chest showed the tumor was reduced in size and no pneumonitis was observed ( Figure 2A ). We administered an inhaled acetylcysteine solution for the symptomatic treatment of dyspnea. However, 1 week later, the patient had a fever with a worsening cough and expectation. Due to the Spring Festival, he did not seek medical attention in time. Then his temperature continued to rise. Only 3 days later, in the emergency department, CT was notable for extensive exudation of both lungs, diagnosis of interstitial pneumonia ( Figure 2B ). The patient's condition continued to deteriorate and he was transferred to the intensive care unit (ICU). His temperature was 42 C, the pulse was 123 beats per minute, mask oxygen was given to the patient. Then his partial pressure of oxygen (PaO2) was only 60 mmHg and the fraction of inspiration O2 (FiO2) was 57%. Serum -ss-d-glucan level was 327.12pg/mL, and the galactomannan was 0.25mug/L. According to the multidisciplinary team (MDT), the patient had a history of previous immunotherapy. CT showed large blurred shadow with unclear margins, and his serum -ss-d-glucan level are high. It was thought to be pulmonary complications related to immune checkpoint inhibitor therapy and possible coinfection. Then methylprednisolone (40 mg per 12 hours) was administered intravenously. And antibiotics such as Compound Sulfamethoxazole Tablets (Trimethoprim 0.16g and Sulfamethoxazole 0.8g per 6 hours), Sulperazon (3g per 8 hours) and voriconazole (0.2g per 12 hours) were empirically administered. After a week, the patient's condition did not improve, and voriconazole was replaced by caspofungin (70mg once 50mg/day). Bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) was performed. On the 12th hospital day, next-generation sequencing (NGS) analysis of BALF specimens identified Pneumocystis jirovecii(PJP), streptococcus pneumonia and cytomegalovirus (CMV). Ganciclovir (375mg/day for seven days   0.25g per 12 hours) was added to his treatment and increased the dose of Compound Sulfamethoxazole Tablets (Trimethoprim 0.24g and Sulfamethoxazole 1.2g per 6 hours). At the same time, the patient with sustained grade III/IV thrombocytopenia, immunoglobulin (25 g/day for five days) was injected intravenously. On the 20th hospital day, the fungal and bacterial sputum culture obtained 7 days earlier grew Aspergillus fumigatus. The patient improved after 23 days in ICU and CT showed reduced inflammation.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 66-year-old man with stage IIIC lung squamous cell carcinoma developed dyspnea and cough 20 days after completing concurrent thoracic radiotherapy and his fourth cycle of tislelizumab plus nab-paclitaxel/carboplatin, rapidly progressing over 10 days to hyperpyrexia (42 °C) and severe hypoxemic respiratory failure.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: Originally diagnosed with stage IIIC (cT4N3M0, PD-L1 TPS 30%) lung squamous cell carcinoma after 4 months of cough and chest pain, the patient completed four cycles of tislelizumab, nab-paclitaxel, and carboplatin, with the fourth cycle synchronized with thoracic radiotherapy (60 Gy in 30 fractions; MLD 8.07 Gy, V20 22.5%, V5 36%), ending in January 2022. Twenty days after completing radiotherapy (20 weeks after starting tislelizumab), he presented with mild cough and dyspnea with tumor shrinkage and no pneumonitis on chest CT, and was prescribed inhaled acetylcysteine. One week later, during the Spring Festival, he developed high fever and worsening productive cough, presenting 3 days thereafter to the emergency department with extreme hyperpyrexia (42 °C), bilateral diffuse pulmonary exudation, and severe hypoxemia requiring ICU admission.
subjective.past_medical_history: Stage IIIC (cT4N3M0) lung squamous cell carcinoma treated with 4 cycles of tislelizumab + nab-paclitaxel/carboplatin and concurrent 60 Gy thoracic radiotherapy; >40-year heavy smoking history (40 cigarettes/day, quit >3 months prior).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for dyspnea, worsening cough with expectoration, and extreme fever (up to 42 °C).

objective.physical_examination: Baseline body weight 71 kg. Upon ICU admission: Temperature 42.0 °C, pulse 123 beats/min, and acute hypoxemic respiratory failure on mask oxygen.
objective.routine_investigations: Initial outpatient dyspnea visit: WBC 14.79 x 10^9/L with otherwise normal hemogram and inflammatory markers. ICU admission arterial blood gas: PaO2 60 mmHg on FiO2 57%. Subsequent ICU course: Sustained grade III/IV thrombocytopenia; hospital day 20 sputum culture (collected day 13) grew Aspergillus fumigatus.
objective.advanced_workup: ICU admission fungal biomarkers: Elevated serum 1,3-beta-D-glucan at 327.12 pg/mL and normal serum galactomannan at 0.25 μg/L. Serial chest CT scans: Initial post-RT CT showed tumor shrinkage without pneumonitis; emergency department CT 10 days later demonstrated extensive bilateral blurred exudative consolidations and interstitial pneumonia. Hospital day 12 bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) metagenomic next-generation sequencing (mNGS): Identified Pneumocystis jirovecii (PJP), Streptococcus pneumoniae, and cytomegalovirus (CMV).

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Checkpoint inhibitor- and radiation-related pneumonitis complicated by severe polymicrobial opportunistic co-infection with Pneumocystis jirovecii pneumonia (PJP), cytomegalovirus (CMV), Streptococcus pneumoniae (all confirmed on day 12 BALF mNGS and serum beta-D-glucan of 327.12 pg/mL), and secondary Aspergillus fumigatus infection in a patient with stage IIIC lung squamous cell carcinoma treated with tislelizumab chemoimmunotherapy and thoracic radiotherapy. Plan and clinical course: Empirically started in the ICU on IV methylprednisolone (40 mg q12h), oral compound sulfamethoxazole (TMP 0.16 g / SMX 0.8 g q6h), cefoperazone-sulbactam (Sulperazon 3 g q8h), and voriconazole (0.2 g q12h, switched after 1 week to IV caspofungin 70 mg loading then 50 mg/day). Following day 12 BALF mNGS confirmation of PJP, CMV, and S. pneumoniae, compound sulfamethoxazole was escalated to TMP 0.24 g / SMX 1.2 g q6h, intravenous ganciclovir (375 mg/day for 7 days, then 0.25 g q12h) was added, and IVIG (25 g/day for 5 days) was given for grade III/IV thrombocytopenia, resulting in clinical recovery and CT regression after 23 days in the ICU.
